chats.answer:
The Starlink Mini can run from a USB-C power source, but it requires USB Power Delivery (USB-PD) at 20V. A standard 5V USB-C charger or USB-A port won't work.

USB-C power requirements

Specification

	

Requirement




USB-C protocol

	

USB Power Delivery (PD)




Voltage

	

20V DC




Minimum power supply

	

100W (20V × 5A) recommended by Starlink




Typical power consumption

	

25–40W




USB-C cable

	

Starlink Mini USB-C to DC power cable




Connector at dish

	

Proprietary DC barrel-style connector

Important: Although the Mini typically consumes only 25–40W, Starlink specifies a 100W USB-C PD source to provide sufficient power for startup and peak loads.

Will different USB-C chargers work?

USB-C output

	

Compatibility




20V / 3A (60W)

	

 Not supported




20V / 3.25A (65W)

	

 Not supported




20V / 4.5A (90W)

	

 Not supported




20V / 5A (100W)

	

 Supported




20V / 5A (140W charger)

	

 Supported if the port provides 20V/5A

Starlink's official documentation specifies a minimum 100W USB-C PD rating. 
Starlink Help Center
+1

Power bank considerations

For portable use, check that the power bank supports 100W from a single USB-C port, not just 100W total across multiple ports.
